headline: Dollar rebounds to 102 before the Fed as oil holds near $116; peso closes at a record 63.95
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.3% to near 102.0 after an early dip to about 101.6, as Brent pared its losses to settle near $116 and resilient US data kept a December Fed hike in view before Wednesday's expected hold, even with the 10-year Treasury yield just under 5%. The loonie held steady on BoC hike bets and the won hit its strongest close of the year, while the yen lagged before Friday's BoJ and oil importers suffered, with the peso at a record 63.95 and the rupee and rupiah at multi-month lows.
drivers: Dollar steadies into a central bank week

The dollar index climbed from about 101.6 in Asia to near 102.0 in New York as investors squared up before the Fed (Oct 28), which is expected to hold at 3.75–4.00% while futures price roughly 75–80% odds of a December hike. EUR/USD fell about 0.25% to 1.1177 and USD/JPY rose about 0.4% to 157.45 as the BoJ is seen holding at 1.25% on Friday.
Oil stays high despite Iran diplomacy

Brent dipped toward $114.5 on reports of Qatari mediation in Tehran but settled near $116, close to six-month highs, as Houthi attacks on Saudi sites continued and Trump said it is nearly decision time on Iran. Oil importers took the hit: the peso fell 33.5 centavos to a record 63.95, the rupee to about 95.20 and the rupiah to about 18,110, its weakest close since June.
Rate-hike bets support CAD, AUD and the won

Markets price about 80% odds of a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Wednesday, keeping USD/CAD near 1.4010 after seven straight loonie gains, and RBA hike odds for Nov 3 rose above 60% before Wednesday's CPI. In Seoul, exporter dollar sales lifted the won to 1,323.1, its strongest close of 2026, despite a 1.46% Kospi drop.
view: Range-bound with a mildly firmer tilt against the euro and oil importers over the next 1–2 weeks: US data are resilient and a December Fed hike is mostly priced, but yields are well off their highs and the BoJ, BoC and RBA are turning more hawkish. I fade the dollar against the yen and loonie into this week's meetings, and back it against the euro, peso and rupiah while Brent sits above $110. A Fed that firmly signals December, or a DXY close above 102.30, would make me dollar-positive across the board; a credible Iran deal that drops oil below $105, or a DXY break below 101.30, would turn me bearish.
ideas: Short from 157.50–157.80, filled today, into a BoJ hawkish pause on Friday, for 155.00, stop 158.60, about 2.8:1.
Short from 1.4030–1.4050, filled at today's 1.4055 high, on an expected BoC hike against a Fed hold, for 1.3880, stop 1.4130, about 1.8:1.
Long: buy dips to 63.70–63.80 while oil above $110 and the payments gap swamp BSP hikes, for 64.30, stop 63.45, about 1.8:1.
review: USD/JPY's 157.50 sell zone filled and is flat, USD/CAD's filled at 1.4055 and is about 0.3% in favour, USD/PHP's long filled at 63.50 and is about 0.7% in favour (target 64.00 missed by 5 centavos), USD/IDR's long is about 0.6% in favour and USD/CHF's short is about 0.3% against; EUR/USD, USD/CNH, USD/KRW and EUR/JPY entries were not reached and every range held. I lower the EUR/USD, USD/CNH and USD/KRW entries and raise the peso target to 64.30.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.25% to near 1.1177 as the dollar firmed in New York; Asian highs near 1.1225 faded.
eurusd.why: The dollar did most of the moving. The euro rose early to about 1.1225 on relief that Moody's spared France a downgrade and on oil's dip, but it reversed as Brent held near $116 and the dollar index climbed about 0.3% to near 102 on resilient US data before the Fed. Weak growth and high energy costs keep the euro vulnerable even with French spreads a little tighter.
eurusd.outlook: Still bearish, but I lower the sell zone to 1.1210–1.1230 because rallies are fading earlier; target 1.1100. A close above 1.1290 would end the call; a hawkish ECB on Oct 29 or a soft Fed are the risks.
eurusd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), the ECB (Oct 29), euro-area flash CPI (Oct 30) and French spreads.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.25% to near 1.3340, and weaker on the euro, as traders squared up before Wednesday's Budget.

view.call: 1.3300–1.3450; buy dips, Budget is the swing factor.

gbpusd.why: Mostly the dollar, plus caution before the Budget. Sterling slipped from Friday's 17-month high against the euro as investors avoided big positions before Chancellor Healey's first Budget on Oct 28, even though 10-year gilt yields fell about 2.5bp to 5.34% on hopes of fiscal discipline. The dollar's New York rebound pushed cable back toward the middle of its range.
gbpusd.outlook: Range 1.3300–1.3450, buying the bottom: BoE hike pricing and a bond-friendly Budget support sterling, but high expectations raise the risk of disappointment. A close above 1.3450 turns me bullish; a gilt selloff after the Budget breaks 1.3300.
gbpusd.watch: The Budget and the Fed (Oct 28), then the BoE (Nov 5).

audusd.note: Down about 0.3% to near 0.7013, back under the 100- and 200-day averages, as the dollar firmed.

view.call: 0.6950–0.7080; RBA hike odds vs firm dollar.

audusd.why: The dollar did the work. RBA Assistant Governor Hunter said the bank is not yet done with inflation, and markets lifted the odds of a Nov 3 hike above 60% from about 22% a week ago, but the Aussie ignored it as US yields steadied and the dollar index rose toward 102. Sellers again appeared near the 0.7033–0.7050 moving averages.
audusd.outlook: Range 0.6950–0.7080: rising RBA hike odds support dips, the moving averages cap rallies. A trimmed-mean CPI at or above about 1.0% q/q on Oct 28 could break it higher; a soft print sends it back to 0.6950.
audusd.watch: Australia Q3 CPI and the Fed (Oct 28), yuan fixings and the RBA (Nov 3).

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.4% to near 157.45 and touched 157.56; the yen was the weakest major before Friday's BoJ.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. After its best week since early September, it gave back ground as the BoJ is expected to hold at 1.25% on Friday and avoid hinting at timing, while the dollar firmed in New York on resilient US data. Lower oil and a 10-year Treasury yield just under 5% limited the rise, and swaps still price about 75% odds of a December BoJ hike.
usdjpy.outlook: My sell zone at 157.50–157.80 has filled; I hold for 155.00 because the BoJ is likely to declare its 2% goal met and flag upside risks, and the rate gap keeps narrowing. A close above 158.60, over the 200-day average, would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), US GDP and inflation data (Oct 29), the BoJ and its outlook report (Oct 30), and Tokyo's 159–160 line.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.3% to near 0.8276 after an Asian dip to about 0.8230; the franc lost its haven bid.

view.call: Short from 0.8240–0.8260; haven risk, Fed hold.

usdchf.why: The dollar led. The pair slipped to about 0.8230 in Asia as oil and Treasury yields eased, then climbed back above the 0.8250–0.8265 resistance as the dollar index rallied to near 102 in New York. The SNB, holding at 0%, has said rate gaps make the franc a cheap funding currency, which caps its gains when markets are calm.
usdchf.outlook: I hold the short from 0.8240–0.8260, now about 0.3% against me, for 0.8100: Iran and AI-led stock stress can revive haven demand quickly. A close above 0.8330 would end the call.
usdchf.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), Iran headlines, European bond spreads and US data (Oct 29).

usdcad.note: Flat near 1.4010 after the loonie's seven-day winning streak, the longest in four years; high 1.4055.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; BoC hike vs Fed hold.

usdcad.why: Two forces balanced. The dollar firmed broadly and US crude slipped about 2% to near $101 early, but markets now price about 80% odds that the Bank of Canada raises rates to 2.50% on Wednesday, its first hike since 2023, after Governor Macklem warned on energy-led inflation. The pair touched my sell zone at 1.4055 and was sold back to about 1.4010.
usdcad.outlook: My sell zone at 1.4030–1.4050 has filled; I hold for 1.3880 because a BoC hike alongside a Fed hold narrows the rate gap. A close above 1.4130 would end the call; a BoC hold, or US tariffs due Oct 30, are the risks.
usdcad.watch: The BoC and Fed decisions (Oct 28), oil, and the US 50% tariffs due on Oct 30.

usdcnh.note: Yuan near a four-year high at about 6.667 offshore after a 6.7162 fixing, the strongest since Feb 2023.

view.call: Sell 6.675–6.685; PBOC lets the yuan grind up.

usdcnh.why: The PBOC kept steering the yuan up, but slowly. Monday's 6.7162 midpoint was the strongest since February 2023, yet 471 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate, the largest weak-side gap since Sept 23, a sign it is resisting faster gains. Exporter conversion and a softer dollar in Asia lifted the onshore yuan to a fresh four-year high before the dollar's New York rebound.
usdcnh.outlook: A managed grind lower: I sell bounces into 6.675–6.685 for 6.630. A fixing set closer to estimates would speed it up; a close above 6.710 or a deeper China stock selloff would end the call.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, US–China headlines and the Fed (Oct 28).

usdhkd.note: Up to about 7.8455 as US yields held near 5% and HIBOR stayed low; close to the 7.85 weak edge.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdhkd.why: Rate spreads keep pushing it up. One-month HIBOR is near 2.7% while US rates sit near 4% on the Fed's 3.75–4.00% range, so selling Hong Kong dollars for US dollars pays. No HKMA intervention was reported, and the dollar's New York rebound added a little.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in the 7.83–7.85 band. A test of 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy Hong Kong dollars and drain liquidity, lifting HIBOR; a dovish Fed would pull it off the weak edge.
usdhkd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), HIBOR and HKMA action at 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.2% to near 1.2808 after September factory output fell 3.9% m/m.
usdsgd.why: Soft local data and a firmer dollar. Singapore's industrial production growth slowed to 3.4% y/y in September from 15.4%, with output down 3.9% on the month, a third straight monthly fall. After last week's softer core inflation, that reduces the case for the MAS to tighten again in January, and the dollar's New York rebound added to it.
usdsgd.outlook: Range 1.2720–1.2830: weaker data remove the tightening tailwind, but the S$NEER stays on the strong side of its band. A close above 1.2830 would open 1.2900; below 1.2720 reopens downside.
usdsgd.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), Singapore's unemployment data and the broad dollar.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 1.5 to 1,323.1 at the Seoul close, its strongest finish of 2026; it touched 1,320.6.

view.call: Sell rallies 1,330–1,335; exporter sales, BoK view.

usdkrw.why: Flows beat risk aversion. Exporters sold dollars before month-end and offshore players sold too, pushing the won past its year high, while BoK Governor Shin's view that the won is undervalued kept bets on gains alive. Foreign investors sold about 700 billion won of shares as the Kospi fell 1.46%, and importers bought dollars in the low 1,320s, which capped the move.
usdkrw.outlook: The trend still favours the won, so I lower the sell zone to 1,330–1,335 rather than chase; target 1,310. A close above 1,345 would end the call; heavier foreign stock selling is the risk.
usdkrw.watch: Samsung and SK hynix results, the Fed (Oct 28), Korea's Q3 GDP and month-end exporter flows.

usdtwd.note: No Taipei trading for Retrocession Day; offshore quotes steady near 32.575.
usdtwd.why: Taiwan's markets were shut for a holiday after Friday's typhoon closure, so the last onshore close is still Thursday's 32.508. Offshore quotes held near 32.575, reflecting last week's foreign selling of Taiwan chip stocks and the Kospi's 1.5% drop on Monday, while a softer dollar in Asia kept it from weakening further.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep fading weakness from 32.50–32.65 for 32.10: export receipts are large and the central bank has said it will act near 32.50 and above. A close above 32.80 would stop it; heavy foreign Taiex outflows on reopening are the risk.
usdtwd.watch: Taipei reopens Oct 27; foreign Taiex flows, TSMC supply-chain and US big-tech earnings, the Fed (Oct 28).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0855/0895 at the 6pm close from 4.0835/0875, but gained on most other currencies.
usdmyr.why: Caution before the Fed. The ringgit opened firmer at 4.0815 as the dollar index dipped early, but analysts cited Trump's hard line on Iran and oil-driven inflation risk for the FOMC, and it ended slightly weaker against the dollar. It strengthened against the yen, pound, Singapore dollar, rupiah and peso.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Exports and Bank Negara support it, and it holds up better than oil-importing neighbours, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed (Oct 28), oil and Bank Negara (Nov 5).

usdphp.note: Peso fell 33.5 centavos to a record-low close of 63.95, its sixth straight record; near 64.

view.call: Buy dips 63.70–63.80; oil, BoP gap swamp BSP hikes.

usdphp.why: Oil and confidence, not rates, are driving it. Brent near six-month highs and Trump's talk of possible renewed action against Iran lifted dollar demand for fuel imports, and economists cited stagflation worries and a widening balance-of-payments gap. The peso opened at 63.535 but sold off all day despite the BSP's surprise 50bp hike to 5.50% last week.
usdphp.outlook: My long filled at the 63.50 intraday low and is about 0.7% in favour. I raise the target to 64.30 and buy dips to 63.70–63.80 while Brent stays above $110; a close below 63.45, likely on an Iran deal, would end the call.
usdphp.watch: Iran headlines and oil, BSP dollar sales near 64, the Fed (Oct 28) and US midterms (Nov 3).

usdidr.note: Rupiah fell 0.4% to about 18,110 (Refinitiv), its weakest close since early June; JISDOR 18,116.

view.call: Long; add 18,050–18,080. MSCI risk, oil, RRR cuts.

usdidr.why: Domestic worries and oil. Investors still weigh MSCI's consultation on cutting Indonesia's market status, Q2's current-account gap of 3.34% of GDP and Indonesian crude near $105, while Bank Indonesia's planned reserve-requirement cuts on Nov 1 and Dec 1 add liquidity. Deputy Governor Destry said BI is in the market, which slowed but did not stop the slide.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long from near 18,000, now about 0.6% in favour, and add on dips to 18,050–18,080 for 18,300. A close below 17,950, likely on a credible MSCI fix or lower oil, would end the call.
usdidr.watch: MSCI's decision process, foreign flows in Jakarta, oil, BI intervention and the Fed (Oct 28).

usdinr.note: Rupee fell 25–29 paise to about 95.20, a third straight loss and 84 paise in three sessions.

view.call: 94.50–95.50; RBI near the top, oil caps the rupee.

usdinr.why: Oil and month-end demand. Brent near $115 lifted oil companies' dollar buying, importers covered month-end needs and foreign portfolio outflows added to demand, so the rupee slid from 94.92 to a low of 95.265. The losses partly reverse its 2.2% rally after the RBI's curbs on speculation earlier this month.
usdinr.outlook: Range 94.50–95.50, now near the top: the RBI is likely to defend 95.50, but oil above $110 blocks a rupee rally. A close above 95.50 would signal a new leg weaker; below 94.50 would extend the RBI-led recovery.
usdinr.watch: Oil and Iran headlines, RBI action near 95.50, foreign flows and the Fed (Oct 28).

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.2% to near 175.98 as the yen was weaker still; high near 176.2.

view.call: Sell rallies 176.50–177.00; weak euro growth, BoJ.

eurjpy.why: The yen was the weaker leg. Both currencies fell against the dollar, but the yen lost more ahead of an expected BoJ hold on Friday, and relief that France kept its Moody's rating gave the euro an early lift. The cross closed near 175.98 (EUR/USD 1.1177 × USD/JPY 157.45), still about 1% below last Monday's level.
eurjpy.outlook: Bearish: sell rallies into 176.50–177.00 for 174.00 while euro growth worries and the yen's haven appeal weigh. A close above 177.80 would end the call; an ECB hawkish surprise is the risk.
eurjpy.watch: The ECB (Oct 29), BoJ (Oct 30), French spreads and risk sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Up about 0.4% to near 23.62 as the yen fell and the yuan held near four-year highs.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. USD/JPY rose about 0.4% before Friday's BoJ meeting while the PBOC kept the yuan near its strongest since early 2023, so the cross rose to about 23.62 (USD/JPY 157.45 ÷ USD/CNH 6.667).
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range, now mid-range. A BoJ hawkish surprise would push it toward 23.3; a break above 23.8 would need USD/JPY near 158.6.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, the BoJ on Oct 30 and risk sentiment.

watch: Next: Taipei reopens and the FOMC starts (Oct 27), the Fed, BoC, Australia CPI and UK Budget (Oct 28), the ECB and US GDP/PCE data (Oct 29), the BoJ and US tariffs on Canada (Oct 30), the RBA and US midterms (Nov 3), the BoE and Bank Negara (Nov 5), plus Iran headlines, oil and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
